description: Helping Hands handheld gripper, Gen 6. Jake (voice): 'It's getting better. I think all the gear mounting and everything should happen actually up above, because I'll be putting it in between my fingers, so I want as little as possible right there in that little niche between my thumb and my index finger. And you see the ones from Generalist? Try just copying those exactly, the gripper shape, with the cutouts and all that stuff. Just identical to those ones. Just try to reproduce them from the images. This is for Gen 6.' Asks: (1) move all gear/servo mounting up above the hand so the thumb-index web stays as empty as possible; (2) reproduce the Generalist gripper fingers exactly from the reference images (shape, cutouts, everything). Build on the latest handheld gripper generation.

results.notes: Jake (voice): 'It looks like there's one wrist strap to hold the whole thing on, and then the other two straps: one goes on the index finger and the other goes on the thumb. Put that as a note. Draw the straps on there, although we won't 3D print them. They should be a separate piece; we could use zip ties for now.' Asks: (1) three straps: one wrist strap holding the whole unit, one strap on the index finger, one on the thumb; (2) model the straps as separate, non-printed parts shown in the viewer/renders (excluded from the print set); (3) give the printed parts strap slots that also fit zip ties for now. .

Jake (voice): sixth reference photo, top-down view of the handheld gripper over a bowl, saved at cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_top.png (source of truth). Shows: camera housing sits on the back of the hand with the lens facing forward/down; the two yellow fingers splay out like an open claw from a central pivot under the housing; each finger has a black rectangular carrier block (with yellow dot markers) bolted along its proximal half; fingers are curved, pocketed with rows of round holes, with a pointed tip and a black dot/insert near the tip. Clear view of the open-jaw spread and finger curvature. .

results.identified_issue: Edited Gen 6 in place (v006_dorsal_drive), as Jake said 'this is for Gen 6'; only finger_profile/perforation/finger_plate params changed, kinematics/housing untouched. Profile: outer crescent to x=+16.5, inner edge wave(z)=-9.2-1.5*sin(360*(z-30)/18) for z 30..90, tip_point unchanged so closed-tip clearance check still passes. Perforations: blind hex pockets both faces, whole-cell-only via minkowski(hex centres ∩ offset(-R) region, hex). tip_start 97->104 (smaller black tip). Ambiguity: the target photo shows the right finger's broad face, which may be the out-of-plane depth face (~25 mm) rather than the motion-plane outline; I modeled it as the in-plane outline and kept 10 mm plate thickness. If Jake says 'deeper', intersect with a Y-Z depth profile. Previews made ad hoc with OpenSCAD camera (no script). Unverified: printability of 3.5 mm-deep 2.4 mm pockets, strength, strap fit.
results.summary: Redrew the Gen 6 fingers to match your Generalist photo: crescent shape, wavy inner edge, rows of small perforations, small black point.
results.detailed_description:
The fingers now follow the photo you sent instead of my first guess. Each one is a yellow crescent that bulges outward and has a wavy inner grip edge with three scallops. There's a small step before the blade and a small black point at the tip, plus a small hole near the point like the one in the photo.

I replaced the big honeycomb through-holes with rows of small hex dimples, about 2.4 mm across and 3.5 mm deep from each face. That leaves a solid 3 mm web in the middle, so they read as the dark dot pattern in the photo and the finger stays stiffer. The lower blade has a solid flat with a grey magnet dot, like the Generalist one. The gears and servo stay above your hand, and the thumb–index web is still empty: all 7 geometry checks pass across the full 0–22° motion, and every part exports as a clean closed mesh.

Two differences from the photo. First, the Generalist fingers look deeper top-to-bottom than our 10 mm plates and have a black rail along the top edge; I didn't add either. Second, the outline is still traced by eye from a small photo, so it's close, not measured. compare_target.png puts the photo beside the model. Tell me whether to make the fingers deeper next.

results.notes: Jake (voice) correction on the cup photo (generalist_gripper_gen6_cup.png): 'It's like pouring the cup, so it's the view from the bottom.' It is the same handheld gripper rotated, seen from underneath while pouring. Ignore my earlier reading that the jaws strap along the index finger and thumb. Use it as the underside view of the fingers and mount. The robot photo (generalist_gripper_gen6_robot.png) is the same gripper on the arm. .

Jake (voice): fifth reference photo, saved at cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_robot.png (source of truth). The same yellow fingers mounted on a robot arm instead of a hand: clearest view of the finger shape. Each finger is an L/hook: a pocketed proximal section that rises from the pivot, then angles down into a long jaw with a hump on the outer back edge and a short pointed tip with a black tip insert. Dense grid of small round/hex pockets on the faces. Fingers pivot on a black plate (with a fiducial tag) under a gray camera housing. The same fingers should work handheld and on the arm. .

Jake (voice): fourth reference photo, saved at cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_cup.png (source of truth, like the others). Shows the gripper grasping a paper cup: the upper yellow jaw is strapped along the back of the index finger and the lower jaw along the thumb, each with a black strap loop, so the fingers drive the jaws directly. Jaws are slim, curved, with rows of small pockets, and pointed tips that hook inward; the cup is held between the curved middle sections. Camera/housing sits back on top of the wrist. .

Jake (voice): 'More than my prompt, these images are the source of truth.' Where the three reference photos in cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_*.png disagree with any spoken description (Jake's or the filer's), follow the photos. .

Jake (voice) correction on the closed-jaw photo: 'It's not touching along most of the finger, it's just the tip here.' So in the Generalist reference, when closed only the pointed tips meet; there is a gap between the inner edges along the rest of the finger. Copy that. .

Jake (voice): third reference photo, front view with jaws nearly closed, saved at cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_closed.png. Shows: when closed, the two yellow fingers meet at the pointed tips and the inner grip edges run almost parallel along most of their length, with interlocking wavy/serrated teeth; the inner faces have a dense dark perforated grid; the fingers pivot from a black plate right under the drive housing, above the back of the hand. .

Jake (voice): second reference photo, side view, saved at cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_side.png. Shows: fingers are long, thick, flat-sided yellow jaws with rows of small rectangular pockets on the outer face, tapering to pointed tips; the hand slides in under a black curved frame with a strap over the index/middle fingers; the pivot and gear plate sit on top of the hand behind the knuckles, and the tall drive/camera housing rises vertically above the wrist. Nothing bulky in the thumb-index web. .

Jake (voice, with photo): 'Just as a reminder, this is the thing you're trying to copy.' Photo saved at cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_target.png: Generalist handheld gripper. Two yellow fingers with a dark perforated inner pattern (rows of small cutouts), wavy grip profile along the inner edge, tapering to pointed tips; black pivot/linkage plate on top with the gear/drive housing stacked ABOVE the hand; strap around the hand; the thumb-index web stays clear. Match those finger shapes and cutouts as exactly as you can for Gen 6. .

results.identified_issue: Lineage: 'latest handheld gripper generation' = Two Finger Gripper/versions/v005_mirrored_gears (Gen 5 per Scripts/publish_designs.py generations map). Gen 6 is versions/v006_dorsal_drive. Interpreted 'up above' as dorsal (+Y, back of hand), since the pivot axes already run along Y: the gears stack on the same axes above the plane, and each jaw is a plate plus a Ø10 column through the housing floor plus an 8 mm hex that keys a separate gear (separate so the jaw can be assembled through the floor). Housing is split into base and lid with 3 M2 bosses so the gears can be installed. Alternatives not taken: moving pivots further forward along Z (still leaves a hub in the web); remote drive by cable (more parts). Finger outline traced by eye mainly from references/generalist/ziptie_1.jpg; honeycomb cells are 4.6 mm across flats with 1.3 mm walls and a 2.2 mm rim. No Generalist dimensions exist. Dropped from Gen 5: outer finger channel (incompatible with honeycomb plates), hard travel stops, adapter part. STLs are gitignored (*.stl), so only the source, checks, previews and viewer_parts.json are committed; run export_models.py to regenerate. Uncommitted working-tree edits to files I don't own (all untracked and from earlier sessions): Scripts/publish_designs.py generations map (+v006 -> Gen 6), references/generalist/GENERATIONS.txt, Two Finger Gripper/README.md. Gen 5 itself and the publisher are still untracked in git, so the remote gets v006 without them. Unverified: cantilever stiffness, pin bending, strap fit, printability, servo interface.
results.summary: Built Gen 6: the gears, servo and housing now sit on the back of your hand, and the fingers are redrawn as Generalist-style honeycomb plates.
results.detailed_description:
The thumb–index web is now empty except for two 10 mm pivot columns. The housing, both gears and the servo moved up onto the back of your hand, 13–59 mm above the finger plane. A check sweeps the whole 0–22° motion and confirms nothing sits behind the pivots in the hand plane. That space is exactly where Gen 5's hub and motor were.

The fingers copy the Generalist ones from the photos: flat yellow 10 mm plates with hexagon cutouts, a knuckle bump on the outside, a lower blade that swings inward, black pointed TPU tips, and two grey magnet dots. I traced the outline by eye, so it's close, not measured.

Three trade-offs: the fingers now hang from the housing on their columns instead of being clamped on both sides; Gen 5's finger groove and hard stops are gone (you attach with straps through slots, and the servo limits travel); and the servo sits on top, so the stack is taller. Open Gen 6 in the Designs gallery and tell me if the finger shape is right before we print.
